ranksNote: These points were measured with different numbers of nodes, so they are not directly comparable.
basis: All 5 nodes run inside one Java process on one machine, so they share its 16 available processors (as reported by the JVM; inside a container this can be lower than the machine's). The speedup cannot exceed 5, the smaller of the node count and that processor count, and other work on the machine lowers it further. For small matrices the scatter of A, the broadcast of B and the gather of C take longer than the multiply they split up, so the parallel run can be slower than the sequential one (a speedup below 1). Each node's compute time is measured on the node, around its multiply only; every other time is measured on the root. 1 untimed warm-up product was run first, so the JIT had compiled the multiply before the timed runs. The timed sequential product runs after 1 warm-up product and the timed parallel run after 2 full products (the warm-up and the sequential product), so the parallel run meets a slightly warmer JIT and processor cache than the sequential product did. Nothing else on the cluster is paused during a run: Experiment 1 calls, MPI collectives, Experiment 2 requests and other experiments can use the same nodes and processors at the same time, and any such work is included in these figures.
rule: For each configured series size, the newest kept run of that size that completed and matched the sequential product. A size without such a run is listed as not run, never as 0. Runs of other sizes are only in the history.
